shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Starting from an even 1A, 1B, 1C bundle, trading 1A for 1B would make my inventory less balanced (0A, 2B, 1C). Since I value variety and currently value all goods equally, this reduces my utility.

Trading 1 B for 1 A changes my inventory from (A:1, C:1, B:1) to (A:2, C:1, B:0), which reduces variety. Since I value goods equally but prefer balanced holdings, this trade does not increase my utility.

Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes me to 3A/0B/1C. Since I value variety and B would become my scarcest good at zero, this reduces variety and does not improve my utility.
I currently have one of each good, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make my inventory less varied without increasing total value.
Trading 1×B for 1×C changes my balanced inventory from (A:1, C:1, B:1) to (A:1, C:2, B:0), reducing variety, which lowers my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C leaves me with 1 A, 3 C, 0 B. This reduces variety and eliminates one good entirely, which lowers utility for my preferences.
I currently hold A, B, and C in equal amounts, so swapping 1 A for 1 B would reduce variety and leave me with more B and no A. That lowers my utility.
I currently have one of each good, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×B for 1×A would make my inventory less varied (A:2, C:1, B:0), which lowers utility.

Starting from an even bundle (1A,1B,1C), trading 1B for 2A gives me more total goods and remains reasonably balanced. The gain of two units outweighs concentrating slightly more in A, so this increases my utility.
